reviews.review: Pretty decent game on its own. But where this game really starts to shine is in the multiplayer. Playing this through with other people is definitely the recommend way to play this as you will be able to play on higher difficulties. Theres also a neat challenge card system where at the beginning of each mission it will allow each player to choose 1 card, the game will randomly choose a card to activate and it works as a sort of mutation system.

The only really good thing in this game is the soundtrack. Well done! The rest is just very average to be honest. There are so many amazing games out there that I do not find this one a good time investment.

This is a relatively early review, since I haven't played the harder difficulties yet.

This is the second aliens game ever made. In the past I would've told anyone who wanted the Aliens Marine experience to just go play Space Beast Terror Fright. That game is still really good, but if you don't want to have seizures while playing a game Fireteam Elite is a good second option. Its a more traditional coop experience in the vein of L4D, but with a class system.

The class system is something I'm a bit iffy on. The game has a combat rating and does have numerical values that you can turn on if you actually want to see what your damage values are like, and the class system ties into this. Classes give you the weapons you can use, and a couple of active abilities to differentiate yourself from other classes, but the way it is used in the late game is to make builds a la Warframe or Destiny. Thankfully, the game isn't a looter shooter. Instead you unlock attachments with different effects, and different guns. All of them are shared across all classes, and you can even get cross-class abilities, and what you slot in determines how effective you are with a pseudo RPG system backend.

The difference can be pretty significant, as you could be missing out on almost 40% increased damage per shot if you don't properly set up your passives, or something like 50% cooldown reduction on an ability. Enemies in the higher difficulties become bullet sponges and these modifiers are needed to actually clear them.

You can also just play normal and ignore all of this, though. And just customize your loadout lightly and ignore the meta. Even though with the way things are, the 'meta' is pretty loose. Most build guides one can look up pretty much tell you "this weapon is what I think is the best, but here's how you'd do this with these 6 other weapons", which is good. It means if I like the Pulse Rifle, I can just build around it, and not be crippled because I didn't pick the objectively superior 90% damage difference XYZ Rifle.

Systems aside, the sound design is great. A lot of the original sounds from the original aliens movies were used. From the hissing of a xenomorph to the sound of the pulse rifle. The environment design is equally amazing, and there is enough enemy variety.

Now for the things I don't like.

There's only 4 campaigns, each 3 missions long, in the base game. With Pathogen giving you another 3 mission long campaign as DLC. 2 Campaigns are in a space refinery, 2 campaigns are basically Prometheus. This means if you like the original Aliens, and you hate the new ridley scott movies, half the game is in the environments you want, the other half is in prometheus inspired environments fighting prometheus based enemies.

I don't mind the fact that these levels are in different environments from what you'd expect from traditional aliens, but they are half of the selectable levels, and in them you end up not fighting the iconic xenomorphs. Now, I'm not complaining that there's enemy variety. You have Xenos,  Synths and Pathogen all with their own fodder enemies and specials. I just wish there were more missions with Xenos as a focus, since the low mission count means you really feel it when you go two missions in a row without a single xenomorph in sight.

The second criticism is that I want more, and there isn't more. I'm surprised there isn't a level in a xeno infested colony. We have the Katanga Refinery Levels, and the hive levels especially are exactly what I wanted, but it means that there's only -one- campaign with face huggers, and that blows.

Give me more. Please.

Absolute blast. 
Pro:
Relatively good story, good visuals, good gun play, many perks and playstyles.
Con:
Strange stutters which only happen when opening new areas.
Lack of players.

Was a pleasant surprise to have a bloody great Aliens game from the start. I am also very impressed with the AI when you want to play alone they are actually able to hold their own. Usually you get complete bone heads on your team and enemy AI is running on god mode. This usually leads to solo play sucking balls looking at you Deathwing not so here well done devs.
